name: THE WATCHMAN'S SHACK
materialIdentity: Bare plank, swept boards, one lamp; very clean and very bare, night (errata 94 A)
note: Room 21, doc 20: Hob's shack, off the back alley. Enterable in Act I, when he is out on his rounds. The confession (doc 48 S4, doc 57 E10) plays here after E9: Hob, the two cups, HOB_C2, and dawn in the window after. THE TALLY MARKS and five silent LISTENs are doc 05's; nothing points at whose room this is. Lines EXTRACTED from the documents by tools/extract-examine.mjs and compiled by tools/compile-room.mjs. Do not edit: change the docs and re-run.

repeat: The wick is trimmed square, and the glass is polished on the inside, which is the side that matters and the side nobody checks.
The brass is worn bright in one place, where a hand lifts it the same way every evening.
then: It's the only well-maintained object I've seen in Consolation.

repeat: Nothing. It is waiting for dark, and it is good at waiting.
Not a sound. It is the only thing in this room that expects to be needed tonight.

LOOK_AT.say: A coat. Eastern cut, twelve or thirteen years out of fashion, and far too good for a night watchman.
repeat: The lining is silk, worn through at one pocket, where something heavy was carried for a long time.
It has been brushed recently and not worn in years. Somebody looks after it for no reason I can see.
Nothing. Good wool keeps quiet on principle.
Nothing. It hangs exactly straight. Even the draft has been asked to leave it alone.

LOOK_AT.say: It faces Main Street. It faces the Improvement Company.
repeat: The glass has been cleaned in one square only, at the height of a man on a stool. The rest of the window may do as it likes.
From here you can see every door on Main Street, and the Company's twice. I don't know what you'd be watching for. I suspect he does.
then: Whoever put this window in wanted to see one particular building.

repeat: Main Street, at the distance a watchman would choose: near enough to hear a door, far enough not to be asked anything.
The Company's door, opening and closing. From in here it is the loudest thing in town.

LOOK_AT.say: Cold. It has not been lit this season.
repeat: Swept out, and the ash bucket empty. A cold stove that someone still cleans.
There is kindling laid in it, dry, and from the dust on it, laid a long time ago.
Nothing. Iron, at the temperature of the room, which is the temperature of outside.
Nothing. A stove that has given up on this season and possibly the next.

LOOK_AT.say: A cot. It has never been slept in.
repeat: The blanket is folded square, with corners you could rule a ledger by. Somebody learned that a long way from here.
There is no dent in the pillow. A man who works nights must sleep days, and he does not do it here.
Nothing. Not a rope under it has been asked to take a weight in years.
Nothing. A cot that has never been slept in has never learned to creak.

overrides.USE: It has been made, military-fashion, every day for years, and slept in — by the look of it — almost never.

LOOK_AT.say: Marks cut into the wall. Thousands of them.
repeat: In fives, the fifth stroke always across. Every group is finished except the last, which is today's.
The oldest are at the height of a standing man's eye and gone soft with handling. The newest are down by the floor. He has run out of wall.
then: Someone has been counting something here for a very long time and has not stopped.

repeat: Nothing. The knife that made these is not here, and neither is the man.
I put my ear to the boards. Wood, and the street beyond it. Nobody is counting out loud.

exits.name: THE DOOR

overrides.CLOSE: It doesn't latch from outside. A watchman's door. Nothing of his was ever protected but the town.

exits.note: Doc 20: the shack's one way out, to the back alley. Doc 49's CLOSE is its one line. NO DOCUMENT WRITES THE DOOR a LOOK or LISTEN, so it is a stub exit as Boot Hill's gate is (doc 36 Q164); the door works, and its LOOK and LISTEN wait for lines.

entrances.note: In by the door, at left, from the alley.

PICK_UP.say: No. Some men you leave exactly where they have chosen to stand.

PUSH.say: He has stood in one place for twelve years. I am not going to be the one who moves him.

USE.say: No. Everybody in this town has had some use of him, and none of them noticed. I will not make one more.
